Text: In Comparable and Comparator, {{c1::Comparable}} defines natural ordering inside the class being compared.
Extra: It requires implementing Comparable<T> and overriding compareTo(T o). Objects of this type can then be sorted automatically via Collections.sort(list) or Arrays.sort(arr).

Text: In Comparable and Comparator, {{c1::compareTo}} is the single abstract method in Comparable that defines natural ordering rules.
Extra: Returns a negative integer, zero, or a positive integer if this object is less than, equal to, or greater than the specified object.

Text: In Comparable and Comparator, {{c1::Comparator}} defines external custom ordering for objects.
Extra: Unlike Comparable, which is embedded inside the class, Comparator allows defining multiple external custom ordering rules.

Text: In Comparable and Comparator, {{c1::compare}} is the abstract method in Comparator used to evaluate two objects.
Extra: It takes two arguments o1 and o2 and returns a negative integer, zero, or a positive integer indicating their ordering.

Text: In Comparable and Comparator, {{c1::Natural ordering}} is the default sorting sequence defined inside a class via Comparable.
Extra: Strings use lexicographical ordering, numbers use ascending numerical order. Sorting non-Comparable elements throws ClassCastException.

Text: In Comparable and Comparator, {{c1::Custom ordering}} is an alternative sort order defined externally using a Comparator.
Extra: It lets you define alternate sort strategies (e.g. sorting strings case-insensitively or by length) or sort third-party classes.

Text: In Comparable and Comparator, {{c1::Sort List object}} is done via Collections.sort(list) or List.sort(comparator).
Extra: Java 8's List.sort() is preferred. To sort naturally with List.sort(), pass "null" or "Comparator.naturalOrder()". Sorting immutable lists throws UnsupportedOperationException.

Text: In Comparable and Comparator, {{c1::Sort by multiple criteria}} chains comparators to resolve equality ties.
Extra: Java 8 provides static and default methods to chain comparisons. E.g. "Comparator.comparing(Employee::getDept).thenComparingDouble(Employee::getSalary)".

Text: In Comparable and Comparator, {{c1::Comparator.comparing}} is a static factory method that creates a Comparator from a key extractor function.
Extra: Primitive variations like "comparingInt" and "comparingDouble" should be used to avoid autoboxing overhead. Key extractor returning null causes NPE.

Text: In Comparable and Comparator, {{c1::thenComparing}} is a default method in Comparator to specify a secondary comparator to resolve ties.
Extra: If the primary comparator returns 0, thenComparing is invoked to decide the order of the objects.

Text: In Comparable and Comparator, {{c1::Reverse order}} swaps the direction of sorting.
Extra: Use "Comparator.reverseOrder()" to reverse natural ordering of Comparable elements, or "comparator.reversed()" to reverse an existing custom comparator.

Text: In Comparable and Comparator, {{c1::Null handling:}} defines how a Comparator orders null values without throwing NullPointerException.
Extra: By default, null elements throw NPE during sort. Java 8 introduced "Comparator.nullsFirst" and "nullsLast" decorators to safely handle nulls.

Text: In Comparable and Comparator, {{c1::nullsFirst}} wraps a comparator to sort null values before non-null values.
Extra: Syntax: "Comparator.nullsFirst(Comparator.naturalOrder())". If both values are non-null, it delegates to the downstream comparator.

Text: In Comparable and Comparator, {{c1::nullsLast}} wraps a comparator to sort null values after non-null values.
Extra: Syntax: "Comparator.nullsLast(Comparator.naturalOrder())". If a null wrapper is auto-unboxed to a primitive inside the comparator, it throws NPE before nullsLast can intercept it.

Text: In Comparable and Comparator, {{c1::consistency-with-equals}} requires that `(x.compareTo(y) == 0) == (x.equals(y))` to avoid duplicate rejection in TreeSet or TreeMap.
Extra: TreeSet and TreeMap rely entirely on compareTo/compare for uniqueness.

Text: In Comparable and Comparator, implementing comparisons using subtraction can lead to {{c1::integer overflow/underflow}} under two's complement arithmetic.
Extra: Wrapping issues reverse the comparison sign bit, leading to contract violations.

Text: In Comparable and Comparator, {{c1::transitivity}} requires that if A > B and B > C, then A > C.
Extra: Violating transitivity in Java 7+ sorting algorithms triggers an IllegalArgumentException.

Text: In Comparable and Comparator, Java uses {{c1::Dual-Pivot Quicksort}} for primitive arrays and {{c2::TimSort}} for object arrays.
Extra: Primitives are value types requiring no stability, whereas objects have identities and require stable sorting.
